questions.statement: If I ________ a lot of money, I ________ around the world.
questions.context: Identifying the structure of Second Conditional.

options.feedback: Correct! Second conditional: If + Past Simple, Would + base form.

questions.explanation:
El Segundo Condicional se usa para situaciones imaginarias. La estructura es: If + Pasado Simple, "would" + verbo en forma base.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If I ________ you, I would study harder for that exam.
questions.context: Using "were" for all subjects in conditionals.

options.feedback: Incorrect. While common in informal English, "were" is the standard for B1 grammar.
Correct! In the Second Conditional, we use "were" for all persons (I, you, he, she, it, we, they).

questions.explanation:
En el Segundo Condicional, el verbo "to be" suele tomar la forma "were" para todos los sujetos, especialmente en la expresión de consejo "If I were you...".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He ________ so tired if he ________ to bed earlier.

options.feedback: Correct! Result (wouldn't be) and condition (went) in Second Conditional.

questions.explanation:
La forma negativa se construye con "wouldn't" (would not) en la cláusula de resultado y el pasado simple negativo (didn't + base) en la condición si es necesario.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If I ________ speak perfect English, I ________ a job in the United States.

options.feedback: Correct! "Could" is the past of "can" used in the condition.

questions.explanation:
Cuando la condición se refiere a una habilidad imaginaria, usamos "could" (pasado de can) en la cláusula del "if".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If we lived in Cartagena, we ________ go to the beach every weekend.

options.feedback: Correct! "Might" can be used instead of "would" to show possibility in the hypothetical result.

questions.explanation:
En la cláusula de resultado del Segundo Condicional, podemos usar "would" para certeza imaginaria, o "might" / "could" para mostrar que el resultado también es solo una posibilidad.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What ________ Bogotá be like if there ________ no traffic jams?

options.feedback: Correct! Asking about an imaginary version of the city.

questions.explanation:
Para imaginar cambios en nuestra realidad actual, usamos el Segundo Condicional. Recuerda usar "were" para "there was/were" en la condición.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
**Sentence A:** If I win the lottery, I will buy a car.
**Sentence B:** If I won the lottery, I would buy a car.

What is the difference?

options.text: Sentence A is in the past.
Sentence A is more likely; Sentence B is purely imaginary.
options.feedback: Correct! First conditional is for real possibilities; Second is for dreams or unlikely events.

questions.explanation:
La diferencia entre el Primer y Segundo condicional no es de tiempo (ambos se refieren al presente/futuro), sino de probabilidad y actitud del hablante hacia la realidad.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
If I **knew** her number, I **would call** her.
What does this sentence imply about the current reality?

options.feedback: Correct! Second conditional always implies the opposite of the current reality.

options.text: I will know her number soon.

questions.explanation:
El Segundo Condicional describe el "mundo de los sueños". Si digo "Si tuviera...", es porque en realidad "No tengo...".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What ________ you ________ if you ________ a ghost?

options.feedback: Correct! Question structure for an imaginary situation.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas hipotéticas se forman con: What + would + sujeto + verbo base + if + sujeto + pasado simple?

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"If I **was (A)** the president, I **would (B)** help **the poor (C)** people more than the government **does (D)**."
questions.context: Identifying errors in complex hypothetical sentences.

options.feedback: Correct! Error found. In formal/B1 grammar, "were" is required in the Second Conditional, especially for "If I were...".

questions.explanation:
Aunque "was" se escucha en el habla informal, los exámenes de nivel B1 (como el Saber 11) exigen el uso de "were" para todas las personas en el segundo condicional.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the most polite and appropriate way to give advice to a friend?
questions.context: Evaluating the use of Second Conditional in advice.

options.text: Study more or you will fail.
If I were you, I would spend more time reviewing the notes.
options.feedback: Correct! "If I were you..." is a standard, polite way to give advice in B1.

options.text: If you don't study, you would fail.

questions.explanation:
El Segundo Condicional es una herramienta social clave para dar consejos de manera indirecta y menos impositiva que usando el imperativo o "must".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Nowadays, many people use cars for short distances. If more people used bicycles for these trips, the air in our cities would be much cleaner. Additionally..."
questions.context: Selecting the best conclusion for a hypothetical argument.

options.text: public health would improve due to increased physical activity.
options.feedback: Correct! Follows the hypothetical logic with a correct Second Conditional result.

options.text: cars are faster than bicycles in the city.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Fact, but doesn't follow the hypothetical argument.

options.text: the government will buy bicycles for everyone.
bikes were invented a long time ago.

questions.explanation: Completar un argumento hipotético requiere mantener la consistencia del tiempo gramatical (usando "would") y seguir la lógica de causa y efecto iniciada en el texto.
